sections.html:
Hagerstown is the seat of Washington County, in western Maryland about 70 miles northwest of Washington, D.C., and 72 miles west-northwest of Baltimore. The 2020 count was 43,527 residents and 19,779 housing units, with 10.2% of those units vacant. The "Hub City" nickname comes from the many railroads that once crossed it.

The city was historically industrial and is now built around logistics, health care and retail. The I-70 and I-81 crossing has drawn warehouses and a large trucking presence. Meritus Medical Center and Hagerstown Premium Outlets are among the larger local draws. When you talk to buyers, say how close the house is to I-70, I-81 and Hagerstown Regional Airport, about 5 miles north.

The city rate was unchanged for the sixth year in a row. The state's reassessment, phased in over three years, raised Washington County residential values 22.8% on average between January 1, 2023 and January 1, 2026. How the transfer tax is split between buyer and seller is set in the contract.

sections.h2: Who bills and when payments are due
sections.html:
Hagerstown owners get tax bills from two places. The Washington County Treasurer's Office does not collect for the City of Hagerstown, so city taxes come from the city at (301) 790-3200.

The county's annual and first semi-annual installments are due September 30, and the second installment is due December 31. Interest on late payments is 1% per month, and annual and first installments go delinquent on October 1. Paying by July 31 earns a 0.5% discount. The semi-annual option is for owner-occupied primary residences, and mortgage lenders are assumed to pay semi-annually unless you tell the lender before May 1.

The county holds a tax lien sale each year on the first Tuesday in June at 9:00 a.m., at the Washington County Office Building, 35 West Washington Street, Hagerstown. The sale puts the lien up, not the house itself.

Delinquency notices go out around March 1, and the accounts are advertised weekly for four weeks. Owners can redeem until a court decree ends the right. The redemption amount is the sale price, 6% annual interest from the sale date and any new taxes. After four months, the buyer of the lien can add legal fees.

All real estate taxes must be current before the deed can transfer, so the settlement attorney collects any unpaid balance from your proceeds at closing. If you are behind, call the Treasurer's Office at 240-313-2110 to get the exact amount before you list or accept an offer.

Do this early. A tax lien sale in June can move a sale from routine to urgent, and a cash buyer who closes before the sale date can clear the balance for you. A cash sale skips lender underwriting and the appraisal, which shortens the path to the settlement table.

The city runs a rental licensing program and a separate vacant structure program, both managed by Neighborhood Services.

  • Any owner who leases a unit must hold a rental license, with a nonrefundable annual fee of $75 per unit.
  • Exterior inspections are annual, and interior inspections occur every 48 months at tenant vacancy.
  • Exemptions include owner-plus-one properties, qualifying new construction within four years, and single-unit rentals to close family members, who must still register.

Vacant structure licensing applies to residential buildings vacant for six continuous months, and to residential structures with a pending foreclosure, which the city treats as blighted vacant structures. A structure the city has placarded as uninhabitable for thirty days is also blighted. Exemptions include active work involving two or more systems and the first year of vacancy while the property is listed for sale with an agent. The program was revised most recently on October 28, 2025.

Contact Code Compliance at 301-739-8577 ext. 805 or codecompliance@hagerstownmd.org for fees, deadlines and owner-change forms. If your house has stood empty, sort this out before you list.

Hagerstown sits where I-70 (east to Baltimore) meets I-81 (north to Pennsylvania and south toward Tennessee), with US 11 and US 40 running parallel. The city has no passenger rail. The Maryland Transit Administration began a feasibility study in February 2023 on extending the MARC Brunswick line. Allegiant Air serves Orlando Sanford, Myrtle Beach and St. Petersburg-Clearwater from the regional airport, and Washington County Transit runs local buses.

Summers are hot and humid and winters cool to moderately cold, with a normal daily mean of 32.9 degrees F in January and 77.6 degrees F in July. The record low is minus 27 degrees F and the record high is 107 degrees F, a swing of more than 130 degrees that a roof and exterior have to handle. A buyer purchasing as is will account for deferred upkeep in the price.

Sellers of one-to-four unit homes give the buyer a state disclosure or disclaimer form. If it arrives late, the buyer can rescind within 5 days. Pass it along with the first draft of the contract, and keep a copy. A disclaimer sells the house as is, but you still have to tell the buyer about latent defects you know of, such as past leaks or a failing furnace.

• A house empty for six months that may need a vacant structure license.
  • A rental with a license and inspection history to check.
  • Back taxes, a lien or a tax sale notice to clear at settlement.
  • Deferred repairs.

Houses that have been empty, rented or neglected are common here, and the city's license rules touch the first two. Gather the license paperwork, the latest tax bills and any city notices before you speak with buyers. Ask the title company to confirm every lien early, so the payoff figure does not change late in the process. Keep every notice you receive in one folder.

1. Call the city and the Treasurer's Office for current tax amounts.
  2. Check whether a vacant structure or rental license applies.
  3. Complete the Maryland disclosure or disclaimer form.
  4. Agree in the contract on who pays the 0.5% county transfer tax.
  5. At settlement, the attorney pays taxes and liens from your proceeds and records the deed.

faqs.q: Does Hagerstown require a license for a vacant house?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Residential structures vacant for six continuous months need a vacant structure license, and a house with a pending foreclosure is treated as blighted. The first year of vacancy while the house is listed for sale with an agent is exempt.

faqs.q: How much is a rental license in Hagerstown?
faqs.a: The annual fee is $75 per rental unit. Exterior inspections are annual and interior inspections happen every 48 months at tenant vacancy.

faqs.q: Does the Washington County Treasurer collect Hagerstown city taxes?
faqs.a: No. The City of Hagerstown collects city taxes and can be reached at (301) 790-3200. The county bills the county portion.

faqs.q: When is the Washington County tax sale?
faqs.a: The county holds its tax lien sale on the first Tuesday in June at 9:00 a.m. The sale is of the lien, not the property.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax in Washington County?
faqs.a: The county transfer tax is 0.5%. How the cost is split between buyer and seller is set in the contract.
